question: Does hook/list distinguish a trusted plugin hook from an installed but unapproved one, and does a default private config report any plugin hooks?

isolation.probe: scratch/hook-list.ts (one handshake, one session/start, one hook/list)
isolation.cleanConfig: scratch/r32-hooklist/config (reminder rows only, no plugin approval)

commands: XDG_CONFIG_HOME=… bun scratch/hook-list.ts (clean config, empty data)
observations: A default private config with no installed plugins returned {"hooks": []}.
With e65-probe installed in the shared data dir and no approval row in the config, hook/list returned {enabled: true, event: sessionStart, handlerKind: plugin, key: plugin:e65-probe:mark}.
With the approval row present, the same row was returned; the catalog carries no trusted_enabled/modified status either way.
The unapproved hook does not run (E65 Arm C), but hook/list reports it as enabled.
result: hook/list cannot distinguish a dormant unapproved plugin hook from an approved one, and reports both as enabled. A gate on handlerKind would refuse sessions for dormant hooks.
branch: P1 cost measured: block-plugin would hit benign dormant hooks
limits: One plugin and one Muse version; bundled plugin hooks were not present in this config.
This measures the catalog, not execution; E65 Arm C measures execution.
The clean config still pins the six reminders off, which is the production private-config shape.
